methodNotes: Walk-forward only: weights at draw t come from same-era draws strictly before t — no full-history rates anywhere.
Raw per-ball frequency is never a weight: the Bayesian grid always shrinks toward the uniform 6/pool baseline.
Eras are scored separately: a 6/45 fold never borrows a 6/49 prior and vice versa.
Primary metric is out-of-sample mean main-number hits per ticket against the era's exact hypergeometric null; max historical score is treated as a search-size artifact (μ + σ√(2 ln M)).
Null-shuffle benchmark: the identical pipeline reruns on synthetic uniform histories (era sizes preserved); matched-M probe statistics compare real vs null at the same variant count.
Multiple testing: BH-FDR across the Route 1 grid per era; the headline claim additionally needs a bootstrap CI that excludes 0 and sign-stable quarter windows.
Route 2 (RNG families) is coverage expansion, not evidence — its winner's curse scales with M.

eraAccounting.reviewBaselineNote: The review brief assumed a 2,700-draw archive (≈330.6 expected hits per ball, σ≈17). The committed archive is 1,892 draws: 654 six-of-45 (2341–2994, to 2014-10-06) and 1,238 six-of-49 (2995–4232). Expected hits per ball are 87.2 (6/45) and 151.6 (6/49); all baselines here are recomputed from the real archive.

route2.note: Search-space expansion only. These variants multiply quickpick coverage across PRNG engines; a hit under a new engine is not evidence of predictive skill — the winner's curse grows with the search size M, and the expected line for the next draw stays the uniform baseline (chance meanHits 0.7347, chance prize rate 1.86% per ticket).

verdict.primaryMetric: out-of-sample mean main-number hits per ticket vs the era chance null
verdict.headline: NO verifiable statistical edge. No walk-forward Bayesian biased-pool variant survives BH-FDR q<0.05, and the real archive's top scores sit inside the 100-history null distribution at the p<0.01 bar (empirical p ≥ 0.01 on every statistic): every max score in the league is an artifact of search size M — for a light-tailed statistic ≈ μ + σ√(2 ln M); for prize-point scores the matched-M empirical null is the ceiling — not a physical bias of the machine.
details: Best 6/45 walk-forward variant bpTop-rolling250: edge 0.0907 hits/ticket, 95% CI [0.0195, 0.1553] excludes 0 but q=0.1079 ≥ 0.05, quarter edges [0.1139, 0.1272, 0.0477, 0.0742] — sign-stable.

Best 6/49 walk-forward variant bpSample-expanding-w2: edge 0.0507 hits/ticket, 95% CI [0.0077, 0.0961] excludes 0 but q=0.2054 ≥ 0.05, quarter edges [0.1104, 0.0667, -0.0781, 0.1037] — sign flips across quarters.
Marginal null-shuffle rows (p in [0.01, 0.05), below the review's p<0.01 bar — reported, not claimed): r1MaxZ_e45 p=0.0495.

Ceiling probe: best of 300,000 uniform variants scored 1001224 league-weighted points. The Gaussian reference μ+σ√(2 ln M) = 45529 deliberately underestimates a prize-point null — a single top-tier match inside M variants dominates the tail — so the authoritative ceiling is the matched-M empirical null: 983795.74 ± 126137.2196 over 100 synthetic histories (real: 1000161 at M=50000, p=0.8515).
